GOLDMAN SACHS
SUMMER ANALYST
Vedanti Kshirsagar
Branch: Computer Engineering
Online Test
Section 1: There were 2 coding questions, both were easy.
Question 1: There is a line consisting of girls and boys. We have to return the number of
pairs that can be formed with adjacent people such that one of them is a girl and the other
is a boy.
Input: GBBBGGBBB
Output : 3
Question 2: In a writing competition, a string is given. Return the character at the kth
position. There were various constraints in this question, one of them was that spaces were
not supposed to be considered.
Examples:
Input: Hello World, k=10
Output: d
Input: ab, k=25
Output : $
Explanation: ab had to be reframed as ab$ba$$ab$$$ba$$$$ab$$$$$
Section 2: This section had all math and logic-based questions. The difficulty level was
medium-hard. There are negative marks for wrong answers so I will suggest do not mark if
you are not sure (unless your fluke game is strong :P).
1

Section 3: This was an advanced coding question. We had 35 mins to solve it. Well, my
keyboard stopped functioning at this point and I don’t remember the exact question
because I was busy panicking :’)
I didn’t solve section 3 at all.
Section 4: This section had questions based on core CS concepts like OOPS, Computer
Networks, OS, etc. I left 2 questions in this section and solved the rest correctly ( I guess).
There were negative markings in this section too.
39 people were shortlisted after this round.
Round 1 - Technical (40 mins)
The interviewer was pretty nice. He started by asking me to introduce myself, he then
asked me about my hobbies because I didn’t include them in my introduction. We
discovered that we both were guitarists and vibed for 10-15 mins :P.
Finally, he asked me this coding question:
https://leetcode.com/problems/trapping-rain-water-ii/
I had to first explain to him the brute force approach. He then asked me to optimize it and
write pseudo-code for the optimal solution on the screen. I did all this correctly. He also
asked me the time complexity of both of my approaches.
Lastly, he asked me whether I had any questions for him. I asked him some questions and
the interview ended. (My suggestion: always ask questions when they ask you to)
17 people were shortlisted after this round.
2

Round 2 - Technical + HR (100-110 mins)
Since my first round was nice, the subsequent rounds were comparatively lenient. Most of
the people had a completely technical round 2.
Here, again the interviewer asked me to introduce myself and then asked me a few
questions about deep learning as I had mentioned it in my introduction (The question was
related to variance and bias, what it is and how it differs in different scenarios).
Then he asked me some DBMS questions:
●
What is normalization
●
Different forms of normalization
●
Which is the best form of normalization (BCNF) with full form.
Then I was asked to design a deque (double ended queue)  using classes and objects. He
expected different functions: add first, add last, remove first, remove last.
I did it using vectors. He said it was right and asked me to do it using linked lists. I did that
too. He was pretty content with the solution.
Then he asked me some HR questions. Here are the ones that I remember:
●
Where do you see yourself in 5 years? (self-explanatory)
●
Goldman Sachs is a finance-based company. Do you know anything about finance?
(Here, I knew about stock markets, investing and trading so I explained that
thoroughly)
●
What are your plans after graduation? (self-explanatory)
●
Why do you want to work at Goldman Sachs?  (self-explanatory)
●
Which domain would you like to work in?  (self-explanatory)
Again, I was asked if I have any questions. I asked some questions that I had.
Umm, everything was very vague after this round. We were sent to a “post interview
break out room” and nothing was specified. No list of shortlisted people was given
for round 3. We were randomly sent to different breakout rooms one by one (some in
groups).
3

Round 3 - HR (10-15 mins)
So, I was the first one sent for round 3. In the previous rounds, I had just one interviewer.
However, in this round, there were three interviewers (ig this happened just with me).
Everyone was asked technical questions in this round too but I got lucky :’)
So, they asked me to introduce myself (again). He then asked me which domains I would
like to work on in case I get selected. So I was supposed to rank them according to my
interests. I said computer networks, web dev and then app dev (Idk why I skipped data
science at this point :/) He then explained how there is not much work in computer
networks related projects in Goldman Sachs. So, I went on to choose web dev.
The other interviewer asked me about my ML related projects and told me to explain them.
He then himself told me what interns do at GS :)))
Again, I was asked if I have any questions so I asked them 2-3 questions.
That’s it. That was the third round for me.
All the interviews were done by 6 pm and the result was sent around 10 pm. 6 people
got selected.
Some tips:
●
First off, don’t be scared or nervous. Keep smiling even if you’re nervous. Don’t let
them know when you’re nervous.
●
Be honest while you answer the questions.
●
Research about the company in advance.
●
Read all previous year experiences from the COC drive as well as gfg archives.
●
Have some mock interviews with your friends and practice how you’re going to
answer some generic questions.
●
Keep your introduction ready and practice saying it out loud before the interview.
●
Know your projects (mentioned on your resume) and the stack used inside out, they
can ask you any twisted questions.
●
Stay hydrated and sleep well before the interview.
4
